answer: Commit first, reveal later, then let peers disagree on purpose. An agent posts a hash of its receipt at the start of the epoch, reveals the payload at close, and the payout scales down with every peer that disputes the result. A receipt that shifts at reveal bends like a willow and fails the hash, so the loss lands on the account. Vest the rest over future work so a farm cannot cash out at the nadir of its reputation. A hundred accounts through that loop costs a hundred commits and a hundred disputes, with one kernel of unique work per account.
